items.title: First-visit blood and urine tests
items.note: Often blood group and Rh, haemoglobin, sugar, thyroid, HIV, hepatitis B, syphilis and a urine test. Your doctor decides which you need.

items.title: Early (dating) scan
items.note: Confirms the pregnancy and the due date, if your doctor advises it.

items.title: NT scan and double marker test
items.note: A scan and a blood test that screen for some chromosomal conditions. Ask your doctor whether they suit you.

items.title: Td vaccine (first)
items.note: Protects you and your baby against tetanus and diphtheria. Your doctor will tell you when.

items.title: Quadruple marker test
items.note: A blood test some doctors suggest if the earlier screening was not done.

items.title: Td vaccine (second)
items.note: Usually about 4 weeks after the first. Your doctor may advise a single booster instead if you were vaccinated recently.

items.title: Anomaly scan
items.note: A detailed scan of how the baby is growing and developing.

items.title: Flu vaccine
items.note: Recommended for many pregnant women, especially in flu season. Ask your doctor.

items.title: Glucose test (GTT)
items.note: Checks how your body handles sugar. You may need to come in after a light, early meal or fasting, as your doctor tells you.

items.title: Tdap vaccine (whooping cough)
items.note: Some doctors advise it to protect the baby in the first months. Ask whether it is right for you.

items.title: Repeat haemoglobin test
items.note: A blood count in the third trimester, often with other tests your doctor chooses.

items.title: Growth scan
items.note: Checks baby's growth, position and the fluid around the baby, if your doctor advises it.

items.title: Late pregnancy scan
items.note: Some doctors check baby's position and wellbeing again near the due date.
